name: Percé
type: village; city or town of Quebec
text: Percé (French pronunciation: [pɛʁse]) is a city located on the shores of the Gulf of St. Lawrence, near the tip of the Gaspé Peninsula, in Gaspésie-Îles-de-la-Madeleine, Quebec, Canada. Percé, member of the association of Most Beautiful Villages of Quebec, is mainly a tourist location particularly well known for the attractions of Percé Rock and Bonaventure Island.

depictions.name: Percé
depictions.text: Percé, Quebec Percé is a small town located in Quebec, Canada. A humble fishing community founded in the 18th century by the French, Percé nevertheless featured a sizable encampment of soldiers. The town also boasted a harbormaster's station, a general store and a tavern, the Sainte-Agathe.
